title: Status
lede: Pyreon is pre-1.0. This page says what that means: how versions change, which parts are mature, which are experimental, and which directions are under consideration. Nothing here is a dated commitment.

items.title: Pre-1.0, one version for everything
items.text: Every published `@pyreon/*` package is released as one fixed version group, so every release gives all of them the same version number. The current version is in any package's `package.json` and on npm.

items.title: Breaking changes are minor bumps
items.text: While the version is `0.x`, a breaking change ships as a `minor` release. Patch releases do not intentionally break APIs. Every consumer-affecting change in a published package carries a changeset, and CI refuses a changeset that declares a major bump.

items.title: Release notes
items.text: Each package's `CHANGELOG.md`, also served by the MCP `get_changelog` tool, so an AI assistant can read what changed between your version and the latest.

items.title: Version skew
items.text: `pyreon info` reports the installed `@pyreon/*` versions and flags skew; `pyreon upgrade` aligns them.

sections.title: What is mature and what is experimental
rows: Reactivity, core, runtime-dom, router, head, server, vite-plugin
Core web framework; the surface most apps use. Pre-1.0 versioning rules apply.
Web meta-framework with build-time mode verification (`verify-modes`) and real-browser end-to-end suites in CI.
Libraries for the web; several also have native runtimes.

sections.title: What "device-proven" means
text: The native targets are measured, not described. The multi-platform docs carry a weighted capability matrix: each category is credited only for behaviour asserted on a real iOS Simulator or Android emulator (a user-visible effect checked by an XCUITest or Compose test), not for code that merely compiles. A CI gate recomputes the headline figure from the table, so it cannot drift from the evidence.

Use the matrix to decide. If the capabilities your app needs are credited at the device level, they are exercised in CI; if not, treat them as unproven. The matrix also shows the weakest rows, such as payments, crash reporting, store release and push.

items.title: Named failures over silent ones
items.text: Code outside the native subset almost always gets a named compiler warning instead of a silent miscompile, and CI gates exist to close the rest.

items.title: Comparisons in one place
items.text: Claims about other frameworks live on one page, including where Pyreon is behind.

items.title: Generated docs are checked
items.text: API references, `llms.txt` and the MCP reference are generated from package manifests and verified in CI, so they do not silently describe an older API.

sections.title: On the way to 1.0: directions under consideration
sections.text: There is no dated 1.0 plan. These directions are not scheduled and may change; they are the biggest gaps the comparison page identifies against the leading app ecosystems.

items.title: Native errors and store submission
items.text: Native errors mapped back to the `.tsx` source, and a documented sign-and-submit path for TestFlight and Play. The rebuild-and-relaunch loop already ships as `pyreon-native dev`.

items.title: A stronger third-party native story
items.text: More first-party service bindings (payments, push providers, analytics) and a documented way for packages to ship their own `native/` sources, building on `useNativeModule`.

items.title: Updates between store releases
items.text: A documented answer using data-driven remote configuration and WebView islands, stated alongside what cannot be done within store rules.

items.title: AI-agent readiness for native projects
items.text: The multi-platform scaffold already writes `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.mcp.json`; the editor-specific rules the web scaffold can generate are not included yet.

items.title: End-to-end test recipes
items.text: Recipes for generated apps and a CI template for building them.

sections.text: Progress on the native side shows in the matrix; everything else shows in the changelogs. If a gap on this list blocks you, say so in a GitHub issue. It is the most useful input we can get.
